assetPolicy: AI-generated or original decorative images, audio and text, and primitive Pygame shapes, are permitted equally. No marks for visual sophistication or paid assets. Assessed code/algorithm assistance follows separately issued school conditions.

years.title: Year 11 Pygame game contract

functional.text: Provide title/instructions, playing, paused and result states. Start, resume, restart and quit through documented keyboard controls.
functional.acceptance: Pause freezes gameplay time and movement; restarting restores initial score, lives, timer and objects.

functional.text: Move one player in four directions using documented keys. Keep the player inside the arena or walkable map.
functional.acceptance: At each outer boundary, another outward move leaves the player in bounds; diagonal speed tricks are unnecessary.

functional.text: Use five collectibles worth 10 points each and three predictable patrol hazards. Collect each item at most once.
functional.acceptance: Collecting the same item twice changes the score only once; collecting all five yields 50 points.

functional.text: Begin with three lives and a 90-second active-play timer. A hazard hit removes one life, returns the player to the safe start and gives 1000 ms hit protection.
functional.acceptance: A hit at 1000 ms leaves two lives; a second collision at 1500 ms leaves two; at 2000 ms it may remove one more.

functional.text: Win by collecting all five items and reaching the exit. Lose at zero lives or zero remaining time. Resolve loss before win if both occur in the same update.
functional.acceptance: With the final item and exit reached while the timer expires, show loss. No further score changes occur after a result.

functional.text: Display score, lives, remaining time, controls and win/loss feedback. Mark player, collectibles, hazards and exit with shape or text as well as colour.
functional.acceptance: A peer identifies each object and reads the current values without an audio cue or colour-only distinction.

functional.text: Use student-written functions with parameters/returns for state changes, collision consequences, scoring and results. Process a one-dimensional list of collectibles; own classes, nested grids and advanced libraries are unnecessary.
functional.acceptance: Explain one function contract and trace removal/collected status for first, last and only remaining collectible.

functional.text: Append the final integer score once per completed run to a local text history. Read valid prior scores and show count, total and first maximum position; show an empty-history message.
functional.acceptance: For [20,0,50,50], count 4, total 120, first maximum index 2. Missing history starts empty. Skip malformed/out-of-range score lines with a warning; a failed write reports failure and gameplay remains usable.
functional.mapping: Unit 1 array processing; sequential files; exception handling

functional.text: Offer two pre-defined difficulty choices; normal patrol interval is 1000 ms and challenge is 750 ms. All other rules, counts, scoring and time remain the same.
functional.acceptance: Unsupported menu keys do not start a run. The selected difficulty survives pause but restart resets the current run.

nonFunctional.text: Usability: instructions visible before play, a clear pause indicator, readable HUD at the agreed 800 × 600 test window and consistent restart/quit controls.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Run a short peer trial; the peer starts, pauses and restarts using only the instructions. Record difficulties and one response.

nonFunctional.text: Reliability: run a two-minute repeatable trial including pause, restart and result states without an unhandled exception. Use a fixed layout and deterministic patrols for tests.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Record the actual build, test sequence, result and any correction/retest. A pause long enough to cross 90 wall-clock seconds must not consume active-play time.

nonFunctional.text: Responsiveness: process close/keyboard events every frame, cap rendering with Clock.tick(60), and avoid blocking sleeps in the game loop.
nonFunctional.acceptance: On the named school reference PC with the required object counts, a pause input is visible within 250 ms in five observations. Record the method and results; investigate misses rather than infer performance from the FPS cap.

nonFunctional.text: Maintainability: meaningful names and constants, one clear responsibility per function/method, comments explaining decisions and a concise README.
nonFunctional.acceptance: A peer finds the score, timer and hazard-interval constants and identifies the scoring function without tracing the whole program.

nonFunctional.text: Portability and resilience: run offline with Python 3 and school-approved Pygame, relative resource paths and primitive-shape fallbacks.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Run from a different parent working directory; remove decorative assets and confirm the full game still works using shapes/text.

nonFunctional.text: Accessibility and assets: sound is optional, colour is never the only signal, and static images/audio/decoration may be made with AI or replaced by Pygame primitives without a marking penalty.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Mute audio and use the shape/text version. Log each external or AI asset, tool/source, date and relevant permissions. Do not assume generated assets are automatically free of third-party rights.

nonFunctional.text: Authenticity and privacy: the assessed game logic, data design and explanations must evidence the student’s own learning. Keep dated versions, backup, and a source/assistance log; use synthetic labels only.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Explain and make a small teacher-selected change to the same project. Asset-generation permission does not decide whether AI code assistance is permitted; the issued school conditions do.

items.description: Identify the audience/problem and compare two design ideas.
Link common FR/NFR IDs to measurable success criteria.
Plan dependencies, checkpoints and the workshop budget.
Design states and function/class interfaces for the common game.
Design the required year-level data structures and file formats.
Provide pseudocode and correct desk-checks for scoring, terminal precedence and the required data algorithms.
Implement state transitions, pause and clean restart/quit.
Implement boundary/collision behaviour, life loss and cooldown.
Implement collection, scoring, timer and result precedence.
Implement the year-level data/architecture requirements: Year 11 list/history processing, or Year 12 maps/OOP/dictionary/search/sort.
Implement validation, file operations and documented failure responses.
Unit tests and traces have independent expectations and actual evidence.
Scenario-independent acceptance cases cover normal, invalid and boundary behaviour; repairs are retested.
Measure quality requirements, including pause, response and asset fallback, on the declared environment.
Judge FR/NFR achievement using actual evidence and acknowledge gaps.
Record a peer acceptance trial and a justified response.
Reflect on process, sources/assistance and one prioritised improvement.

years.scope: One fixed arena, five collectibles, three predictable hazards and a results/history screen.
excluded: 3D, VR/headset integration, multiplayer, online services or accounts
Procedural worlds, A* pathfinding, physics engines, complex platform jumping or advanced enemy AI
Database integration, crafting/inventory systems, shops, dialogue trees or extra level editors
Marks for animation, original artwork, audio production, asset quantity or paid software
years.prerequisites: Before issue, teach the Pygame event/draw/timing loop, Rect collisions and the provided shell in existing lessons. Core programming prerequisites come from the textbook. If that preparation is missing, re-plan class time before release; do not add mandatory home development.

functional.text: Complete a map by collecting its five items and reaching the exit. Map 1 completion advances to map 2; map 2 completion wins the game. Lose at zero lives or zero remaining time. Resolve loss before completion if both occur in the same update.

functional.text: Display score, lives, remaining time, controls and win/loss feedback. Mark player, collectibles, hazards and exit with shape or text as well as colour.
functional.acceptance: A peer identifies each object and reads the current values without an audio cue or colour-only distinction.

functional.text: Implement two supplied 8-row × 10-column tile maps as independent two-dimensional lists. Use tile codes 0 floor, 1 wall, 2 start, 3 exit, with exactly one start and exit per map. Clear map 1 to enter map 2; five collectibles per map, three hazards, a fresh 90 seconds per map and carried score/lives.
functional.acceptance: A wall move does not change position; changing map 1 does not mutate map 2. Maximum game score is 100. A failed map check shows a useful error instead of starting an invalid game.

functional.text: Create a small student-authored actor base class and Player/Hazard subclasses with attributes, methods and shared movement/bounds behaviour. Instantiate objects and override a relevant update method. Separate game rules from drawing.
functional.acceptance: Explain inheritance and abstraction using actual calls; each subclass uses shared base behaviour and its own update. Merely importing a ready-made Sprite class does not supply this evidence.
functional.mapping: Unit 3 classes; objects; methods; inheritance; abstraction

functional.text: Use a dictionary keyed by item ID for item metadata. Write a linear search to locate an item ID in the active item list and a taught bubble, insertion or selection sort to order up to ten valid history scores for the results report.
functional.acceptance: Search [A,B,C] for B gives index 1, for Z gives a documented not-found result. Sorting [30,10,20,10] ascending yields [10,10,20,30]; empty and single inputs work. Dictionary lookup alone is not the search evidence; sorted()/sort() alone is not the algorithm evidence.

functional.text: Load and validate the map data; append one final game score to text history and show the ordered history-score report. Handle missing/malformed files and failed writes under a documented policy. History accepts integer scores 0–100: skip malformed/out-of-range lines with a warning, treat a missing file as empty and show a useful save-failure message. Report at most the latest ten valid scores.
functional.acceptance: Wrong dimensions, an unknown tile or duplicate start prevent play with a useful message. A completed game is saved once; restarting does not duplicate the previous result.
functional.mapping: Unit 3 modular structure; exception handling; test evidence
